message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| 2 | **Gather Parts** | All components must fit together. | Use a PC build checklist or a site like PCPartPicker to avoid incompatibilities. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| 4 | **Open the Case** | Access to motherboard, PSU, drives. | Remove side panels, unscrew screws. |
| 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Provides power to all components. | Place PSU with the fan facing down or up depending on case airflow. Secure with screws. |
| 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other components. | Align standoffs, screw in the motherboard. |
| 7 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount of paste. Attach cooler per its instructions. |
| 9 | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Open DIMM slots, align notch, press until clicks. |
|10 | **Mount Storage Drives (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot; for 2.5”/3.5” drives, secure in drive bays. |
|11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Visual output & gaming performance. | Insert into the top PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect any required PCI‑e power cables. |
|12 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | PSU 24‑pin to motherboard, 8‑pin CPU power, GPU power, SATA power to drives. |
|13 | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer. | SATA data cables to motherboard, M.2 connectors already seated. |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics. | Tuck cables behind the motherboard tray, use zip ties or Velcro straps. |
|15 | **Check All Connections** | Prevent hardware damage. | Verify no loose screws, all cables firmly seated. |
|16 | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Screw side panels back on. |
|17 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Confirm hardware is recognized. | Power on, enter BIOS (usually Delete/F2). Check CPU, RAM, storage detection. |
|18 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Use a USB flash drive with Windows 10/11 or Linux installer. Follow on‑screen prompts. |
|19 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works optimally. | Download latest drivers from manufacturer sites (GPU, chipset, etc.). Run Windows Update. |
|20 | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify stability and performance. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark) and monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
- **Motherboard** – Compatible chipset (e.g., B550, Z590)
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (minimum 8 GB)
- **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070 or AMD Radeon RX 6600/6700
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (500 GB+) + optional HDD (1 TB)
- **PSU** – 650 W (80+ Gold) or higher
- **Case** – Mid‑tower with good airflow
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/ AIO liquid cooler

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short‑circuit** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; double‑check standoffs. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, use quality thermal paste, keep dust out. |
| **Component not detected** | Re‑seat the component, check BIOS settings, update firmware. |
| **Power issues** | Verify PSU wattage, use correct cables, test PSU with a multimeter or PSU tester. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build compatibility checker.
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help.
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and GPU manuals.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and aesthetics. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for specific help. Happy building!
